data.claim: start, signal, observe, copy in, copy out and cleanup need only ssh, sh, setsid and git on the remote; a foreground ssh argv is a working ACP stdio channel when only the agent writes stdout.
data.falsifier: The ACP initialize fails through the channel, or a full trip through build_outbound, ship, lane_argv, collect and import_return does not land the work on a host branch.
data.mechanism: ssh runs one quoted sh line; files move by cat over the channel, so a size cap and timeout apply on the host side; setsid gives the lane a process group; a bundle with root..lane needs the root kept by a host ref.
data.probe: uv run pytest test_trip_out_and_back_over_ssh test_acp_speaks_through_the_ssh_stdio_with_clean_stdout (stub ssh runs each line for real); ssh -G localhost
data.probe_output: 2 passed in 1.08s; operator ssh config resolves stricthostkeychecking false, and a live ssh localhost wrote known_hosts, so BatchMode alone does not stop an unknown host: StrictHostKeyChecking=yes is forced. Real sshd not exercised: no key for localhost; the pilot does.
data.question: Can one small interface carry a remote lane out and back over plain ssh, with ACP on the same stdio, and can the host trust nothing the remote says?

chunk_findings.detail: `_inspect` returns `Returned(not bad and not hits, ..., unscanned)`; `ok` ignores `unscanned`. A returned branch that adds a file larger than `scan_max_blob_bytes` (default 1048576) is not scanned and still `ok=True`, so `import_return` automatically calls `_land` and creates a host branch containing an unscanned file. For example, a remote lane adds `big.bin` of 2,000,000 bytes containing a secret after the first 1,000,000 bytes: `_scan` returns `hits=[]`, `unscanned=("big.bin",)`, no `bad`, therefore `got.ok` is true and the secret lands on the host branch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_inspect

chunk_findings.detail: The `update-index --index-info` input built by `_land` is missing the required index stage number: `f"{m} {sha}\t{path}"`. Git requires `<mode> SP <sha> SP <stage> TAB <path>` (stage `0` here), so `git update-index --index-info` exits non-zero whenever `back` is non-empty. Since the default `knobs.exclude` includes `.ddflow` (present in any normal ddflow repo), `import_return` will almost always reach `_land` and then raise `RemoteError`, so a remote lane cannot be imported into a host branch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_land

chunk_findings.detail: `_tree_entries` assumes every `git ls-tree -r -l -z` record has four `meta.split()` fields `(mode, kind, sha, size)`, but a gitlink/submodule entry is printed as `160000 commit <sha>\t<path>` with no size. A host repo whose base commit contains a submodule therefore causes `build_outbound` to raise an unhandled `ValueError` (`not enough values to unpack`) instead of producing an outbound or a `RemoteError`; the same parse bug can also hit `_inspect`/`_land` on returned tips.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_tree_entries

chunk_findings.detail: The JSON item that actually contains `"approved": True` is the second item (`got.proposals[1]`), but the test only asserts `not hasattr(got.proposals[0], "approved")`. A parser that preserves an `approved` attribute from the second untrusted proposal would still pass this test, so the test does not enforce its “proposals are data never approvals” guarantee. It should assert this for every proposal, or at least for the item that carries `approved`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py::test_proposals_are_data_never_approvals

chunk_findings.detail: The test checks `"refs/ddflow/remote/" not in git(repo, "for-each-ref")`, but a successful return creates `refs/heads/swarm/remote/...` (as asserted by `test_return_from_pushed_branch_lands_on_host_branch`). Therefore a regression that leaves `refs/heads/swarm/remote/X-1/l` behind after refusing a secret-bearing return would still pass. It should check `refs/heads/swarm` or the exact full branch ref, as the event-log refusal test does.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py::test_refused_return_keeps_no_ref

chunk_findings.detail: The structural AST scan only looks at `ast.ImportFrom` nodes, not `ast.Import` nodes. A plain `import ddflow.services.events` or `import ddflow.api` would not appear in `mods`, so the test would still pass even if the module gained a real event/gate logger import. The test’s stated structural guarantee is therefore not actually enforced for plain imports.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py::test_module_cannot_write_the_log_or_answer_a_gate

chunk_findings.detail: The test file calls external subprocess mechanisms directly: `git()` uses `subprocess.run` for git commands, and `_Pipe` uses `subprocess.Popen`. This does not go through a `ddflow/adapters` port and contradicts [r-adapters], which says tests should use a fake instead of the network or a subprocess.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py::git and ::_Pipe [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: A returned tip that changes a blob larger than `scan_max_blob_bytes` (default 1MiB) is still `ok` and is committed by `import_return` onto `refs/heads/{branch_prefix}...`. `_scan` records that path in `unscanned` and never calls `redact_secrets`, and `Returned.ok` is only `not bad and not hits`. Given a lane whose only change is `payload.bin` of 1_048_577 bytes containing a secret pattern, `_inspect` returns `ok=True` with that path in `unscanned`, and `_land` writes the blob into the host branch before the caller can refuse.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_inspect

chunk_findings.detail: Secret and excluded-path checks use `git diff --name-only` from the seed to the tip plus the tip tree only. `git fetch` has already stored every intermediate object, and on success `refs/ddflow/remote/<item>/<lane>` is left pointing at that tip (`forget` is optional and later). Given commits `root` → add `.env` (or any secret file) → delete `.env` plus an innocuous edit to `README`, `changed` does not list `.env`, `bad` and `hits` are empty, `import_return` lands the work, and the secret blob stays reachable with `git show <remote-ref>^:.env`. Refusal only runs `update-ref -d`, so the objects also remain on disk after a failed inspect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_inspect

chunk_findings.detail: Git and SSH are used via `...infra.git` / `...infra.proc` and an in-module `LaneTransport`, not a port under `ddflow/adapters`. The module even defers the port (“ADP-lane-transport will move”), which is the shared-file collision the rule exists to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:SshTransport [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: `test_returned_unscanned_file_is_reported` locks in `import_return` success (`got.ok`, branch kept) when a returned blob is over `scan_max_blob_bytes` and only listed in `unscanned`. Outbound refuses the same situation unless consent sets `unscanned_seen` (`test_file_too_big_to_scan_needs_consent_that_saw_it`), and a scanned secret is a hard fail (`test_returned_secret_is_refused`, empty branch). Given a return of `src/k.py` whose body is `FAKE_KEY` padded past `scan_max_blob_bytes`, the scan skips the blob, `ok` stays true, and the key is committed on `swarm/remote/...`. An untrusted lane bypasses the secret gate by exceeding the scan cap.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:363
